question: Does God know and value me?
truth: You are a beloved child of God with eternal worth.
title: God Knows and Loves You
speaker: Alan T. Phillips
summary: You are a child of God, known and loved by Him. Your worth remains through both accomplishments and setbacks. Jesus Christ offers hope, healing, and purpose wherever you are in life.
application: Education, success, relationships, and personal achievements can bring meaning, growth, and opportunities into our lives. Yet our lives are made up of much more than the things we achieve or the circumstances we experience. This message teaches that our deepest worth is something every person already has: we are children of God, known and loved by Him. Whether life brings great success, unexpected setbacks, or a path that looks different from what we hoped, our worth remains.

question: Why am I here?
truth: Your life has divine purpose, even when you cannot yet see the whole plan.
title: Your Divine Nature and Eternal Destiny
speaker: Dale G. Renlund
summary: You came to earth with divine identity and eternal potential. Remembering who you are can help you make choices with greater purpose as you learn to understand and follow God's plan.
application: Life does not always unfold in the way we expect, and it is natural to wonder where we fit or what gives our lives meaning. This message teaches that our purpose is greater than any one role, accomplishment, or stage of life. As children of God, we are here to learn, grow, make meaningful choices, and develop our divine potential. We may not understand the whole journey at once, but knowing our lives have eternal purpose can bring meaning to where we are right now.

question: Why is Jesus Christ central to everything?
truth: Jesus Christ is not merely part of the answer—He is the answer.
title: The Answer Is Always Jesus Christ
speaker: Russell M. Nelson
summary: Jesus Christ is the center of Heavenly Father's plan. Through His teachings, Atonement, Resurrection, and covenant power, we receive forgiveness, healing, direction, peace, and the hope of eternal life.
application: Everyone searches for meaning, direction, peace, and hope in different ways. This message teaches that Jesus Christ offers something deeper than guidance for a single moment: through His life, teachings, sacrifice, and Resurrection, He made forgiveness, healing, change, and life after death possible. His example also shows us how to love, forgive, serve, and draw closer to God. Understanding who Jesus Christ is helps us understand why His life and teachings can bring lasting meaning and direction to our own.

question: Can Jesus Christ really help with my burdens?
truth: Jesus Christ is not an added burden; He is the source of relief.
title: Jesus Christ Is Not Our Burden; He Is Our Relief
speaker: David J. Wunderli
summary: Following Jesus Christ does not mean carrying every burden alone. The Savior offers strength, rest, and relief as we come to Him and allow His grace to support us through difficult seasons.
application: Life can bring burdens that leave us unsure of what to do next or where to turn for help. This message teaches that Jesus Christ understands our pain and invites us to turn to Him for strength, comfort, wisdom, and direction. His help can come in different ways—sometimes through peace within a difficult season, and sometimes through the strength and guidance to take important steps forward. Turning to Him reminds us that we do not have to navigate life's hardest moments without hope or help.

question: Can I change after making mistakes?
truth: Because of Jesus Christ, your past does not have to determine your future.
title: Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning
speaker: Patrick Kearon
summary: The Savior offers more than one chance to begin again. Through repentance and His Atonement, setbacks, weakness, and sin can become turning points instead of permanent definitions of who you are.
application: There are moments when we may wish we had chosen differently, responded differently, or could begin again. This message teaches that Jesus Christ makes change and repentance possible, so a mistake does not have to become our permanent identity or determine the direction of our future. Through Him, we can seek forgiveness, learn from our experiences, make things right where possible, and continue becoming better. A new beginning does not mean the past never happened—it means the past does not have to be the end of our story.

question: Do I have to be perfect before God can help me?
truth: Worthiness is faithful direction, not flawless performance.
title: Worthiness Is Not Flawlessness
speaker: Bradley R. Wilcox
summary: God does not expect immediate perfection. Through the grace of Jesus Christ, we can repent, improve, and continue growing while still receiving divine help along the way.
application: Growth rarely happens all at once. We learn through effort, experience, mistakes, repentance, and continuing to try. This message teaches that God does not wait for us to become flawless before He helps us; through Jesus Christ, we can receive grace and strength while we are still learning and becoming. This does not make our choices or efforts unimportant—it means imperfection does not prevent us from moving forward with Him.

question: How can I find peace when life is still difficult?
truth: Peace comes through Jesus Christ, not through perfect circumstances.
title: Finding Personal Peace
speaker: Henry B. Eyring
summary: The Savior's peace can enter our hearts before our circumstances improve. As we receive His peace, we can find strength in times of fear, strengthen others, and carry hope into troubled situations.
application: Peace does not always mean that uncertainty, fear, or difficult circumstances immediately disappear. This message teaches that Jesus Christ can bring a different kind of peace—one that gives us strength, hope, and reassurance while life is still unfolding. As we come to know Him through prayer, His teachings, and our experiences with Him, we can develop greater trust that we are not navigating life alone. His peace can help steady us as we decide what steps to take next, even when every answer has not yet come.

question: What should I do when anxiety or conflict surrounds me?
truth: Prayer may not remove every storm immediately, but it brings divine support within it.
title: Prayers for Peace
speaker: Henry B. Eyring
summary: Turning sincerely and repeatedly to Heavenly Father can bring peace and abiding support. Prayer helps us place our fears before God, recognize His presence, and move forward with greater spiritual steadiness.
application: Prayer gives us a place to bring what is already in our hearts—our gratitude, questions, fears, hopes, and uncertainty—to God. This message teaches that prayer is more than asking for a particular outcome; it is a way of building a relationship with Heavenly Father and learning to recognize His guidance. Answers may come differently or at a different time than we expect, but prayer can help us seek understanding, receive strength, and move forward with greater trust. We do not need perfect words to begin; sincere communication with God is enough.

question: How does God guide me personally?
truth: God guides us through the Holy Ghost as we seek, recognize, and act.
title: Promptings of the Spirit
speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
summary: As we seek God's guidance, the Holy Ghost—who helps us recognize truth and God's direction—can guide us in knowing how to move forward. As we learn to recognize His promptings and act on them with faith, we can grow in our ability to recognize God's guidance in our lives.
application: Important decisions do not always come with obvious answers. This message teaches that God can guide us through the Holy Ghost, who can help us recognize truth, feel peace, and receive quiet direction toward what is good. Learning to recognize that guidance can take time, and it does not require every impression to feel dramatic or unmistakable. As we pray, learn God's teachings, use good judgment, and act on the understanding we receive, we can become more confident in recognizing His direction.

question: How can I avoid confusing my own wishes with revelation?
truth: Revelation works within God's truth, commandments, and appointed order.
title: A Framework for Personal Revelation
speaker: Dale G. Renlund
summary: Personal revelation is guidance from God through the Holy Ghost. It works within the truths and commandments God has already revealed, helping us seek His direction without confusing our own desires with His guidance. Prayer, scripture, humility, and obedience can help us learn to recognize that guidance.
application: God invites us to seek His guidance rather than navigate life's important questions alone. This message teaches that personal revelation is guidance from God received through the Holy Ghost, the third member of the Godhead, whose role includes helping us recognize truth and drawing us toward Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ. Elder Renlund explains that this guidance works within a framework that includes prayer, scripture, God's commandments, and what He has already revealed. Understanding this helps us seek God's direction with greater confidence while recognizing that answers and understanding may come gradually, line upon line.

question: How can I remain faithful during overwhelming trials?
truth: Faith in Jesus Christ creates spiritual steadiness before the storm is over.
title: Steady in the Storms
speaker: Henry B. Eyring
summary: Faith in Jesus Christ gives us a sure foundation when life feels uncertain. As we trust Him, follow His teachings, and seek His guidance, He can give us strength, hope, and peace through life's storms.
application: As we turn to Jesus Christ with faith, seek the guidance of the Holy Ghost, and follow His teachings, He can strengthen us when life feels uncertain. Being steady in Christ does not mean that difficult circumstances simply disappear. It means building our lives on a sure foundation, allowing His strength, guidance, hope, and peace to help us move forward with faith.

question: What can I hold onto when I feel discouraged?
truth: Hope in Christ sees beyond the pain of the present moment.
title: The Triumph of Hope
speaker: Neil L. Andersen
summary: Hope in Jesus Christ is more than wishing for easier circumstances. It is confidence that His promises are real, His Resurrection is certain, and His peace can sustain us while answers are still unfolding.
application: Hope can be difficult to hold onto when life changes unexpectedly or when we cannot see how something will turn out. This message teaches that hope in Jesus Christ is more than expecting every circumstance to become easier; it is trusting that the present moment is not the whole story. His Resurrection gives us reason to look beyond loss, disappointment, and uncertainty with confidence that God's promises extend beyond what we can see right now. Hope does not ask us to ignore what hurts; it reminds us that what we are experiencing right now does not define the whole future.

question: How can I respond when conflict or disagreement happens?
truth: True discipleship is revealed most clearly in how we treat one another.
title: Peacemakers Needed
speaker: Russell M. Nelson
summary: Jesus Christ teaches us to respond to others with compassion, respect, self-control, and love. Peacemaking does not mean we must always agree; it means choosing to reduce contention while still standing for what is right.
application: Disagreement is a natural part of relationships and life, but the way we respond can either deepen division or create space for understanding. This message teaches that Jesus Christ showed a better way to treat one another—with compassion, respect, self-control, and love. Being a peacemaker does not mean agreeing with everything, ignoring harmful behavior, or giving up appropriate boundaries. It means seeking ways to reduce unnecessary hurt while still standing for what is right and treating others with dignity.

question: How can what I have to offer make a meaningful difference?
truth: The Savior can multiply a willing offering, even when it feels small.
title: Here Am I, Send Me
speaker: Susan H. Porter
summary: Like the child who offered loaves and fishes, we can offer what we have with a willing heart. Jesus Christ can magnify our sincere efforts and use them to bless others in ways we may not always see.
application: It can be easy to wonder whether what we have to offer is enough to make a difference. This message teaches that meaningful service does not begin with having the most time, resources, influence, or ability; it begins with a willingness to offer what we can. Just as Jesus Christ multiplied a small offering of food to bless many people, He can magnify sincere efforts in ways we may not immediately see. What matters is not comparing our contribution with someone else's, but recognizing that what we are able to give can still bless another person's life.

question: What should guide the choices I make today?
truth: An eternal perspective gives greater meaning to daily decisions.
title: Think Celestial!
speaker: Russell M. Nelson
summary: Daily decisions can shape the direction of our lives. As we remember Jesus Christ and choose His way of living, we can see our decisions with an eternal perspective and find greater purpose, peace, and true joy throughout our mortal journey.
application: Life can change in ways we planned for and in ways we never expected. This message invites us to look beyond the pressure to have every part of life figured out and consider what helps us grow closer to God and become who we are capable of becoming. "Thinking celestial" means viewing our choices, relationships, challenges, and opportunities with an eternal perspective. It does not require everyone's journey to look the same; it helps us seek God's direction for the life and circumstances we are navigating now.
